original.target_description: Experiment 1: trustworthiness relationship requested with r-squared; printed R2 is for the joint by-face model of both judgment types, not a separately reported trustworthiness-only model.

notes: Identity independently verified from article header: What Is Typical Is Good: The Influence of Face Typicality on Perceived Trustworthiness; Carmel Sofer, Ron Dotsch, Daniel H. J. Wigboldus, Alexander Todorov; DOI 10.1177/0956797614554955. Primary published research article, Psychological Science 2015, 26(1), 39–47, copyright 2014; canonical text includes methods, results and references. No target PDF was supplied. Only assigned unfinished fields are populated; other fields and replication are placeholders. Target analytic model is unresolved: R2 = .99 describes the joint regression with DFT, DFT-squared, judgment type and interactions. The neutral locator describes trustworthiness alone. Participant group counts are 24 per judgment type; 11 faces were each judged three times. These are different roles, not an explicit critical-model analytic N. No N inferred from regression df or from multiplying face and judgment-type counts.
